references_named: Yves Klein, Zones of Immaterial Pictorial Sensibility (1959-1962)
Yves Klein, the receipt-burning ritual on the Seine (1962)
rationale: This is a near-perfect execution of the DNA. The mechanism enacts the idea: the receipt is the only material proof, and burning it (with a CSS animation) nullifies the serial in closure while the page persists nothing — reload proves the transaction never existed. The Klein reference is precise and the NFT critique is implicit in the structure rather than stated, exactly the cheerful-cynic double-coding the DNA rewards. The build is minimal (P3), the chance/order axis is legible (per-visit zone number as chance, ritual as order), and the work is materially distinct from the catalogue — no Klein, no receipt-burning, no anti-NFT gesture exists there.
